lines.text: In 2026, hospital-run practices lost a median $314K per full-time doctor.
lines.say: Hospital-run practices lost over three hundred grand per doctor in twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: So why do hospitals keep buying practices?
lines.say: So why do hospitals keep buying practices?

lines.text: By January 2026, 82% of US doctors worked for hospitals or corporations, up from 62% in 2019.
lines.say: By January twenty twenty-six, eighty-two percent of doctors worked for hospitals or corporations, up from sixty-two percent in twenty nineteen.
Hospitals alone employed about sixty percent.

lines.text: First, facility fees. In a CMS example, Medicare paid $119 for a chemo infusion in an office, and $341 in a hospital department.
lines.say: First, facility fees. In a C M S example, Medicare paid one hundred nineteen dollars for a chemo infusion in an office, and three hundred forty-one in a hospital department.

lines.text: That's $222 more for the same service.
lines.say: That's two hundred twenty-two dollars more for the same service.

lines.text: In July 2026, CMS proposed cutting pay for more imaging at older off-campus sites to 40% of the hospital rate.

post.title: Hospital-run practices lose ~$314K per doctor. Why buy more?
post.ig:
In 2026, hospital-run practices lost a median of about $314K per full-time doctor (Kaufman Hall, Q2 2026). So why do hospitals keep buying practices?

By January 2026, 82% of US doctors worked for hospitals or corporations (59.7% for hospitals), up from 62% in 2019.
Facility fees: in a CMS example, Medicare paid $119 for a chemo infusion in an office vs $341 in a hospital outpatient department.
Referrals and orders: a 2019 Merritt Hawkins survey found the average doctor brought affiliated hospitals about $2.4M a year. In July 2026, CMS proposed paying older off-campus sites 40% of the hospital rate for more imaging.

Sources: Kaufman Hall Physician Flash Report Q2 2026, PAI-Avalere 2026 report, CMS outpatient rules (2026, 2027 proposed), Merritt Hawkins 2019.
News and education, not financial advice.
